newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's first family bungee jumps through crisis.
newsitem.headline: Peru's first family bungee jumps through crisis.

text.p: While their father pondered his next move in Peru's hostage crisis, the children of President Alberto Fujimori went bungee jumping on Saturday.
The four arrived with a group of friends and about 10 bodyguards wearing civilian clothes at a bridge overlooking the Pacific Ocean in the smart Lima district of Miraflores.
Twenty-one-year-old Kenji, Fujimori's youngest son, was the first to make the 115 foot (35 meter) plunge. Hiru Alberto, 25, went next and Sachi Marcela, 23, followed.
"I'm the crazy one in the family," Hiru Alberto told Reuters after his jump.
Fujimori's eldest child, 27-year-old Keiko, who has acted as Peru's first lady since her parents' 1995 divorce, declined to jump.
"The first lady is too scared, that's why she didn't jump," Hiru joked.

Fujimori's children made no comment on the hostage crisis which has gripped Peru since Dec. 17 when a group of armed Marxist rebels stormed a cocktail party at the Japanese ambassador's residence taking hundreds of VIP guests hostage.
